findings.problem: The 'unsafe' step is justified only by a red sticker 'jump too big', and the picture does not support it. The rejected vertex (0.6207, jump 0.0091 from b) sits well inside the bracket and is actually closer to the true minimum (0.62) than the golden probe that replaces it (0.6228). The lesson's real test is 'the step is not shrinking fast enough' (0.0091 is more than half of the previous step 0.0049), but neither number is on screen, so a learner sees a sensible-looking jump rejected for no visible reason and may conclude Brent distrusts large jumps in general. 'Too big' is also not what the lesson says (a jump that is merely larger than half the last step).
findings.fix: Show the comparison the rule uses: two small bars or tags 'last step 0.0049' and 'this jump 0.0091', then the sticker 'not shrinking' (or 'jump bigger than half the last step'). At minimum rename the sticker to 'step not shrinking' to match a3-brent's wording.
findings.evidence: s7@10.0 (red cross on the vertex ring at 0.6207, sticker 'jump too big'). Node: A3.brent(4).steps[3] has vertex 0.6207, x 0.6228, last step |0.6116 - 0.6067| = 0.0049, jump |0.6207 - 0.6116| = 0.0091; lesson algo-p3-x-06.js brentRun: 'the step is not shrinking fast enough'.

findings.problem: Caption 3, 'Near the bottom it shrinks to a tiny triangle.', uses the word that names a specific Nelder-Mead move (shrink, the last resort introduced one scene earlier), while the chip row on the same screen reads 'shrink 0' to the end (29 reflect, 19 expand, 36 contract, 0 shrink). The triangle gets small through contractions, not shrinks. Scene 8 has just taught 'Nothing works? Shrink towards the best', so a learner is told two opposite things at once. The tag 'squeeze' is the right plain word.
findings.fix: Reword the caption to 'Near the bottom it squeezes to a tiny triangle.' (or 'it keeps pulling in until the triangle is tiny') and keep 'shrink' for the move only.
findings.evidence: s9@7.5 and s9@9.6 (caption 'shrinks' beside chip 'shrink 0'); s9@12.2 final chips reflect 29, expand 19, contract 36, shrink 0 (matches lesson RUN6: 84 rounds, 198 evaluations, in 26 + out 10, no shrink).

findings.problem: Captions 2 and 3 run ahead of what the picture shows. Caption 2 ('The triangle stretches along the valley', from 3.2 s) is on screen while the first rounds are all contractions (s9@3.4: rounds 3, 'contract 3', no stretch tag; the real run starts 1i 2i 3i 4i 5i). Caption 3 ('Near the bottom it shrinks to a tiny triangle', 6.6-9.8 s) starts while the triangle is still mid-valley and bigger than at the start (round 56 is its widest at about 0.27 across, versus 0.14 at the start; it is below 0.03 only after round 76, about 9.2 s). For about 2.5 s the caption states the opposite of the picture.
findings.fix: Start caption 2 at about 5.2 (just before the 'stretch' tag, rounds 29-35) and caption 3 at about 8.6-9.0 (when the 'squeeze' tag shows, rounds above 72); fill the gap with a shorter caption such as 'It follows the curve.' or leave it blank.
findings.evidence: s9@3.4 (caption 'stretches', chips reflect 0 expand 0 contract 3); s9@7.5 (round 58, caption 'near the bottom', ring far from the star); s9@9.6 ('squeeze' tag, round 79). Node on A3.NM_ROS: size 0.141 at round 0, 0.330 at 12, 0.269 at 56, 0.032 at 76, 0.0014 at 84.

findings.problem: The shrink demo (11.6-13.6) is run on the same convex bowl with no hint that it is hypothetical, but lesson 3.15 says 'on a strictly convex f a shrink can never happen' (the lesson's own shrink example uses Rosenbrock). The numbers are right (G (2.75,1.25) -> (3.5,1.5), W (3.75,0.25) -> (4,1), new best f 0.49), yet the picture continues the real round-4 triangle as if the next round shrinks, and the 'last resort' tag does not say 'imagine'. A learner can leave believing this run shrinks, and scene 9 then shows 0 shrinks.
findings.fix: Make the tag read 'last resort, rare' or 'what if nothing works?' and fade the contour star/triangle slightly; keep the caption as an if-sentence ('If nothing works, shrink towards the best.'). Optionally say 'rare' in the shrink chip's tag.
findings.evidence: s8@12.5 and s8@13.5 (shrink chip red, 'last resort' tag, triangle continues from round 4). Lesson algo-p3-x-08.js, 'Shrink: the last resort': 'On a strictly convex f a shrink can never happen'. Node: A3.nmShrink(NM_BOWL.rounds[3].next) = B (4.25,1.75), G (3.5,1.5), W (4,1).

findings.problem: The first caption says 'Flip its worst corner through the middle', but 'the middle' is never labelled and is not the middle of the triangle: it is the midpoint of the best side B-G (lesson: centroid of every vertex except the worst). The storyboard/code builds a grey 'middle' tag (midTag) but it never appears (the layout drops the optional item), so the diamond is unlabelled while a learner is being told to flip through 'the middle'. The corner letters B, G, W are also never defined: only 'worst' is in the caption; 'G' (good, the middle-ranked corner) and 'B' (best) are left to be guessed.
findings.fix: Make the 'middle' tag show (give the layout room at 2.1-3.0 s) and reword the caption to 'Flip its worst corner through the midpoint of the other two.' Add one short legend once at 1.4-2.2 s ('B best, G good, W worst') or spell the three tags 'best', 'good', 'worst' for the first round.
findings.evidence: s8@2.3 and s8@2.7 (grey diamond on the B-G side, no tag, caption 'through the middle'); scene-08-moves.js lines 234 and 340 (midTag exists, o is 0 when LAY[0].mid is missing). Lesson a3-nm-ops: 'C is the average of every vertex except the worst'.

findings.problem: The first card is titled 'gain per unit of z', which says the opposite of what it shows. The bars are how much z gains per unit of the variable (x +3 means each extra x adds 3 to z; the lesson calls it 'reduced cost' / 'how much z rises per unit'). Read literally, 'gain per unit of z' is a quantity per unit of profit. In a first-time learner's head this makes the +3 / +2 / +1 / -1 numbers hard to anchor.
findings.fix: Retitle the card 'z gained per unit' (or 'extra profit per unit of x / y'), keeping the row labels as the variable names.
findings.evidence: s4@3.4, s4@7.4, s4@12.2 (card title 'gain per unit of z' over rows x +3, y +2 / y +1, s2 -1 / s2 -4/5, s1 -3/5). Lesson a3-simplex step 2: 'how much would z gain per unit?'

findings.problem: The names s2, s1, 'y-axis', 'machine' and 'material' are used without ever being introduced. s1 and s2 (slack: unused machine hours / raw material) appear in the gain card at the second and final corners ('s2 -1', 's2 -4/5', 's1 -3/5') and the ratio card has a row called 'y-axis 15' (the rule x >= 0). 'machine'/'material' name the two rules, but scene 2 labelled them only '1: x + 2y <= 10' and '2: 3x + y <= 15', and scene 4 shows no rule labels, so the link depends on the line turning orange. The lesson steps that define slack and the three rules (a3-slack, the x, y >= 0 rule) are deliberately skipped, so the video needs a minimal substitute.
findings.fix: Label the rows in words a learner can read off the plot: 's2' -> 'material left over', 's1' -> 'machine left over' (or draw a tiny slack icon), and 'y-axis' -> 'x runs out'. In scene 2 add the rule names to the labels ('1: machine x + 2y <= 10', '2: material 3x + y <= 15') or in scene 4 add small 'machine' / 'material' tags on the lines.
findings.evidence: s4@7.4 and s4@10.2 (gain rows 'y' and 's2', ratio rows 'machine 3' and 'y-axis 15'); s4@12.2 (rows s2 -4/5, s1 -3/5). Values verified: at (5,0) z = 15 + y - s2, at (4,3) z = 18 - 3/5 s1 - 4/5 s2; ratios 3 and 15 are correct.

findings.problem: Three things in the lesson's problem statement are missing, so the polygon is not fully explained. (1) The third rule x, y >= 0 is never shown: the polygon simply stops at the axes while the area beyond them is not tinted red like the other illegal regions (left of the y axis at y < 5 is white), so the learner cannot tell why those plans are not legal. (2) What x and y are (units of product X and Y, earning 3 and 2) and what rules 1 and 2 are (machine hours, raw material) is never said; they are only 'x', 'y' and two inequalities. (3) The lesson's vocabulary is 'feasible region' and 'constraints' (also the boss quiz wording); the video says only 'legal region' and 'rules'.
findings.fix: Add a small grey tag 'x, y >= 0' on the axes and tint the outside of the axes the same light red (or add a third rule label with a short tick on both axes); give the rule labels names ('1: machine hours', '2: raw material' on a second line or in the checker card); change the tag to 'feasible (legal) region' once.
findings.evidence: s2@5.3 and s2@11.8 (polygon edges on the axes with white, untinted space left of the y axis and below the x axis; tag 'legal region'); lesson algo-p3-01.js 'A factory problem' lists three constraints (machine hours, raw material, x, y >= 0) and step titles 'Each rule cuts the plane in half' / 'feasible region'.

findings.problem: The width stat counts by interpolation, so for 0.4 s each step it shows widths the algorithm never produces, while the bar under the axis is still at the old bracket. The bracket-width card reads 0.1245 at s5@9.6 (true values 0.125 then 0.0625) and 0.382 -> 0.236 passes through values like 0.31 in scene 6.
findings.fix: Snap the text to the old value until the span has moved and then to the new one (switch the text at the bump), animating only the bar and the card's pop.
findings.evidence: s5@9.6 (stat 0.1245 with the span still at width 0.125); scene-06-golden.js lines 232-236 (lerp of the width text).

findings.problem: The orange star (the minimum) is shown from the first second of both Nelder-Mead scenes, whereas the video-wide convention (and scene 5) is that the minimum star appears only once found. Here the algorithm 'does not know' where it is, but the picture hands the answer to the viewer; scene 9 even labels it 'minimum' beside the start triangle.
findings.fix: Keep it (it makes progress readable) but mark it as the viewer's aid: a grey tag 'target (hidden from the algorithm)' for the first 2 s, or draw it as a hollow ring until the end and fill it orange when the triangle arrives.
findings.evidence: s8@2.3 (star at (3.5, 2.2) at 0.6 s), s9@2.2 (star plus 'minimum' tag before the run); storyboard CONVENTIONS: 'the optimum / minimum is an orange star that only appears once found'.

findings.problem: Caption 3 says 'it homes in much faster than golden section' from 6.4 s, but the evidence (golden width 0.146 vs Brent 0.029, same 7 evaluations) is only shown at 11.2 s, during the 'unsafe' caption. Caption 1 ('Fit a parabola through the three points', until 3.2 s) also stays on screen over the jump itself (ring, probe, evaluations 4 at 2.2-3.2 s) that caption 2 describes.
findings.fix: Move the comparison cards (or a small 'golden after 3 steps: 0.236' tag) next to caption 3 at about 8.6 s, or reword caption 3 to 'Repeat: the bracket collapses fast.' and keep the comparison for the end. Start caption 2 at about 2.2 s.
findings.evidence: s7@2.9 (caption 1 over the jump to x), s7@7.7 (caption 3, no comparison), s7@12.7 (compare cards golden 0.146 / Brent 0.029). Numbers verified: golden width after 4 steps 0.1459, Brent 0.0292.

findings.problem: The middle-ranked corner is blue ('G'), while lesson 3.14 colours best / middle / worst green / orange / red ('middle' is amber in its figure) and 3.15 calls it 'good'. The video's own colour roles (blue = the point we look at) justify the choice, but the storyboard-vs-lesson difference is unflagged, and the lesson uses both 'middle' and 'good' for the same corner.
findings.fix: Decide once (storyboard note, and the 'G' legend suggested above) and keep the word 'good' with the letter G in the video.
findings.evidence: s8@2.3 (B green, G blue, W red); lesson algo-p3-04.js 'A triangle, not a point' (middle = amber) and algo-p3-x-08.js ('best, good, worst').
